patch.objective: Treat a seizure lasting 5 minutes or more as status epilepticus: protect the airway, check glucose, give a benzodiazepine first

sources.cite: Neurocritical Care Society. Emergency Neurological Life Support: Status Epilepticus Protocol, version 6.0 (updated July 2024)
sources.note: Relayed from the CCRN Adult case status-epilepticus-after-craniotomy, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-14 (summarizing fetch with quotes): status epilepticus is 5 minutes or more of convulsions, or two or more without return to baseline; adults with IV access get lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV up to 4 mg, repeated once after 3-5 minutes if not effective; check glucose without delaying treatment; urgent control with levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (maximum 4,500 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg/kg (maximum 1,500 mg) or valproate 40 mg/kg (maximum 3,000 mg) if seizures continue after adequate benzodiazepines; refractory status needs intubation and an anesthetic infusion; start continuous EEG; respiratory decompensation is more common in untreated status than with benzodiazepines.

sources.cite: Glauser T, Shinnar S, et al. Evidence-based guideline: treatment of convulsive status epilepticus in children and adults. Epilepsy Curr. 2016;16(1):48-61. doi:10.5698/1535-7597-16.1.48
sources.note: Relayed from the CCRN Adult case status-epilepticus-after-craniotomy, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-14 through the AES summary page (the full article and its chart were not read): stabilization 0-5 min; initial benzodiazepine 5-20 min (IM midazolam, IV lorazepam or IV diazepam); second therapy 20-40 min (fosphenytoin, valproate or levetiracetam, none clearly better); third therapy from 40 min with continuous EEG.

brief.situation: 08:00 on a neuroscience progressive care unit. Mr. Hale, 56, 80 kg, is one day after a craniotomy for a left frontal meningioma. He is on levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily; the 06:00 dose is charted as held while he was nil by mouth. He is awake and talking.
handover: Unit status epilepticus protocol (standing order): for a convulsion of 5 minutes or more, lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV, maximum 4 mg a dose, repeated once after 5 minutes if still seizing; point-of-care glucose; notify the provider. Further antiseizure loading needs the provider's order.
Arterial line in. 2 L oxygen by cannula. Suction at the bedside.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Some steps take a minute or more, and the seizure goes on while you work.
Partway through you are asked to write what is happening and what comes next. A debrief scores what you did.
